blocks.title: Privileged Access Management exam shortcuts
items: Admin rights needed for one task only → JUST-IN-TIME
Grant elevation only for the required window.
Example: Engineer receives admin access for 30 minutes.
Shared admin password should not be known by everyone → PASSWORD VAULT
Store and broker the credential securely.
Example: PAM checks out and rotates the admin password.
Temporary cloud workload needs credentials → EPHEMERAL CREDENTIALS
Use short-lived credentials rather than long-term secrets.
Example: A workload receives a token valid for one hour.
Question asks how to control powerful admin accounts overall → PAM
PAM is the broader privileged-access control framework.
Example: Admin sessions are approved, recorded, and time-limited.
blocks.example: First determine whether the scenario is asking who the user is, what they can do, how they authenticate, or how privileged access should be controlled.

questions.q: An engineer receives administrator privileges for only 30 minutes to complete a maintenance task. Which PAM capability is this?
questions.explanation: Just-in-time permissions provide temporary elevation only when needed.

questions.q: A shared administrator password should be hidden from users, checked out securely, and rotated automatically. Which capability is best?
questions.explanation: Password vaulting securely stores, brokers, and rotates privileged credentials.

questions.q: A cloud workload receives a credential that automatically expires after one hour. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Ephemeral credentials are short-lived and automatically expire.

questions.q: A company wants a platform that approves, records, monitors, and controls administrator sessions. Which broad solution is this?
questions.explanation: Privileged Access Management controls and monitors privileged accounts and elevated access.
